landing.eyebrow: Open tool for citizen oversight · public data in EN / FR / ES
landing.title: Follow public money with evidence you can verify.
landing.subtitle: Load public contracts, budgets or any table the government publishes. CivicLens checks the data quality, shows you how to clean it, answers questions in SQL, points out contracts that deserve a second look, and writes a report you can share — every step explained and repeatable.

developers.title: Automate CivicLens with the API
developers.subtitle: Everything you do in the app — upload, clean, query, model, report — is one HTTP call away, for any table. Machine fields stay in English; human text follows Accept-Language (EN or ES).

upload.title: Upload a file and wait for the job
upload.body: Send a CSV, XLSX or flat JSON file (up to 50 MB). The answer is 202 with a job; poll it until it succeeds. Progress comes with a phase and a percent.

explore.title: Check the domain and ask questions in SQL
explore.body: See which domain pack CivicLens suggests and how it mapped the columns, then run the generated questions — or your own read-only SQL — on the table data.

results.title: Train a model, read the findings, get the report
results.body: Train a model for the target (with its baseline, leakage warnings and fairness check), read the dashboard's written findings and download the report as HTML or PDF.

code.upload: Upload the file (the job processes it in the background)
code.poll: Poll the job until status is succeeded
code.domain: Suggested domain pack and column roles
code.query: Run read-only SQL on the table data
code.model: Train the prediction model (default target: the domain's or the table's yes/no column)
code.overview: Dashboard findings, one sentence per chart

auth.title: API keys
auth.body: Send X-API-Key with each call. Keys are scoped (datasets:write, recipes:write, models:run, reports:read) and revocable from the admin console. The public demo also accepts anonymous calls.

language.title: Languages
language.body: Accept-Language: es or en. Ids, codes, numbers and SQL never change with the language; titles, explanations and findings do. Data values are never translated.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: Every error is an RFC 7807 problem with a stable code (e.g. dataset.not_found) and a localized title and detail.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Uploads up to 50 MB, kept 24 hours. Heavy calls (uploads, recipes, models) are rate-limited per minute; a 429 says how long to wait in Retry-After.
